subject: Johnson v. Johnson, 2025CV936 — hearing script and fallbacks (P31 Forge / styled memo)

body.text: Camden County Superior Court · Chief Judge Scarlett. Read aloud once before you leave. Do not state a statute or case unless it matches your filed papers and you have re-checked the cite.
1. Identity line (every time you stand or unmute)
"Your Honor, William Johnson, pro se, in case 2025CV936."
Shorter
"William Johnson, pro se, 2025CV936."
2. Opening scripts (pick one)
A. General (record + motions + readiness)

"Your Honor, William Johnson, pro se, in 2025CV936. I ask the Court to look at the documentary record on discovery, the pending motion for protective order, and the issues I raised about the written order record. I am ready for your questions."
B. If the judge asks what you want first

"I want the Court to rule based on the filed record: my March twenty-sixth production and specific objections, the pending protective order in PeachCourt filing E-NLC3ERUM, and the contempt issues only to the extent they match signed filed orders in the clerk's file."
C. If the judge asks you to go first on contempt

"Your Honor, before any remedy, the basis for contempt has to match the written filed record. My position is in my briefing: the third complaint and what actually appears as a signed order in the file. I am not asking the Court to take my word for it — I am asking the Court to compare the complaint to the clerk's file."
(Statute / cases: say only what you filed, e.g. O.C.G.A. 9-11-58(b) and Tate / Shirley — after you verify labels.)
D. If the Court opens with discovery only

"I served supplemental responses and production on March 26, 2026. My objections were numbered and specific, not blanket. I filed a motion for protective order — E-NLC3ERUM — and that motion is still before the Court."
3. One-sentence theme (reset)
"The record shows good-faith compliance and a pending protective-order motion; contempt should not be based on objections and productions that are already in the file."
Softer variant
"I am asking the Court to decide this on the documents, not on labels."
4. Fallbacks — procedure and pacing
Compound question — "Your Honor, may I answer that in two short parts?"
Mind goes blank — "Your Honor, one moment — I want to answer accurately. May I refer to my notes on that single point?"
Judge talks fast / you missed a word — "Your Honor, may I have that last question repeated once? I want to answer what you actually asked."
Counsel interrupts — (Look at the judge.) "Your Honor, I will yield — I was not finished with my answer to the Court's question if the Court wants me to continue."
Judge cuts you off — "Understood, Your Honor. In one sentence: [theme or one fact]."
Wrong lane — "Your Honor, let me correct course — my answer to that issue is: …"
Need a second — "Your Honor, may I have a brief pause to organize my response?"
Asked to speak to counsel — "I will meet and confer in good faith by email as the Court directs; on the record I address the Court."
5. Fallbacks — discovery attacks
You did not produce — "I produced on March 26, 2026 — email to jenn@mcghanlaw.com with the Drive link. The specific objections are in my written responses — they are not refusals without grounds."
Blanket objections — "They were not blanket — each request had a stated basis. I can walk the Court through any single request number if helpful."
Trade secrets / AI / therapy notes — "Those categories were asserted with specific legal bases in writing — privilege and scope — not as a stall."
Protective order — "That is why I filed the motion for protective order — PeachCourt E-NLC3ERUM — so the Court could rule on scope before anyone treats good-faith objections as contempt."
6. Fallbacks — contempt / order basis

Do not wing it — "Your Honor, my position is exactly what I filed: compare the third complaint to the signed written order in the clerk's file. I do not want to misstate the statute on my feet — it is in my paper at [tab / exhibit]."
Which order? — "The order the contempt motion relies on — I am asking the Court to confirm what is actually filed as the controlling written order for that paragraph."
Verbal or everyone knew — "My understanding is that contempt has to trace to a clear, written, filed requirement. I am asking the Court to tie any finding to that record."
7. Fallbacks — fees / sanctions / bad faith

"Your Honor, any fees have to be tied to conduct the Court finds sanctionable after evidence. My objections and production timeline are in the record; I do not concede that fees follow from good-faith discovery positions."
8. Fallbacks — P31 Labs / EIN / hidden money

"P31 Labs, Inc. is a Georgia nonprofit — incorporated April 3, 2026, EIN 42-1888158 assigned April 13, 2026. The CP 575E is in my folder. There are no shareholders and no distributions. The updated business documentation matches what I produced in discovery."
9. Fallbacks — board / directors
"The Articles name directors; a formal organizational board meeting has not happened yet. That is normal for a brand-new nonprofit — it is not the same as hiding a structure."
10. Fallbacks — transcript (Evett)

"Your Honor, I ordered the transcript and paid seventy-five dollars and eighty cents on March 19, 2026. The reporter has been non-responsive. I am asking the Court how it wants that reflected or how I should proceed so the record is complete."
11. Fallbacks — ADA / pacing
"Your Honor, I am AuDHD and pro se. If I need a short pause or to read a one-line note so my answer stays accurate, I am asking for that accommodation."
12. Closing scripts
Court ruled from the bench
"Thank you, Your Honor. For the record I understand [one plain sentence]. I will comply with the written order when I receive it."
Under advisement
"Thank you, Your Honor. I will stand by for the Court's written order and comply."
Clarification
"Your Honor, may I ask one clarifying question so I do not accidentally violate what the Court intends?"
Preserve error (only if your research supports it)
"Your Honor, for the record I preserve my prior positions in my filed motions and responses."
13. Hard stops (do not do)
Full names of minor children in any public context. On the record: initials only if the Court requires it.
Arguing a statute or case from memory — point to your filing instead.
Long speeches — three sentences, then: "That is my position unless the Court wants more detail on a specific point."
14. After you sit down (not for the record)
Note one-sentence outcome, next deadline, clerk task, time you emailed counsel if ordered.
Hearing Ops PWA: https://ops.p31ca.org
This memo is a speaking aid, not a filing. Align every legal claim with your docket entries and submitted papers.
